title: Introduce Slimline Layout Mode with Predictive Column Prioritization and Pulse Resize
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: Customers with high-cardinality tables and limited screen real-estate report cognitive overload and frequent manual column resizing. Existing density modes reduce padding but do not re-prioritize columns or provide a quick multi-column resize gesture. This ticket proposes a new 'Slimline' layout mode that: 1) applies tighter tokenized spacing, 2) uses a predictive priority model (client+telemetry heuristics) to compress or collapse low-importance columns, and 3) introduces a 'pulse resize' gesture to apply proportional width adjustments across a contiguous column group.
background: Design system currently supports compact/comfortable/dense tokens and a single-column resize affordance. UX research sessions (Q4 2025) revealed two recurring patterns: (a) users expect the table to 'make space' for primary columns instead of leaving manual resizing as the only option, and (b) power users want a fast, low-mouse-movement gesture that adjusts multiple columns to reach a readable layout. Engineering has also requested clearer heuristics for column collapse to avoid surprises when autoscaling in Dedicated and Private deployments.
proposal: Introduce a Slimline mode toggle on table chrome and a per-table 'priority map' that can be seeded by headers, pinned state, and usage telemetry. When enabled, the runtime will: - Reduce horizontal padding and tighten type tokens (token set change) - Collapse or minify columns flagged as low priority (visual collapse to icon or summary) - Expose a pulse-resize handle (double-drag or modifier + drag) that proportionally reallocates width across a selected column range - Provide an undo affordance and accessible keyboard equivalents (Alt+Arrow to cycle priority/resize). The design will ship with clear microcopy explaining collapse behavior and an opt-out for deterministic apps.
design_notes: Tokens: introduce --rdw-table-slim-padding and --rdw-table-slim-gap. Visual states: collapsed column shows header pill with tooltip and concise summary (max 2 tokens). Animation: 120ms ease-in for collapse/expand, 240ms proportion for pulse-resize. Accessibility: ensure expanded accessible name and aria-expanded on collapsed cells; keyboard pulse via Shift+Arrow applies proportional adjustments. Telemetry: record column_prios, user overrides, and collapse events for iteration.
acceptance_criteria: Slimline toggle visible in table settings and persists per-user in Console
Predictive prioritization honors: pinned, sorted, and user-edited columns over telemetry suggestion
Pulse-resize gesture works with mouse and keyboard and updates widths proportionally across selected range
Collapsed columns present accessible fallback (aria labels and keyboard reveal) and do not drop data from DOM for screen readers
Design tokens for slim mode are added to the design system token file and have cross-breakpoint values
Telemetry captures collapse/expand and pulse-resize usage to allow A/B evaluation
